honesty_note: 26 REAL WebSearches, every query actually executed; all recorded titles/URLs/snippets are from returned results (verbatim or close paraphrase of the returned summary text), none fabricated or recalled from memory. Verdicts: C25, C29, C31, C32 = COLLISION (each with >=1 directly-named published technique reproducing the functional effect, plus saturated forced-hit counts). C30 = the one GAP, and it is the answer to the mandate: it is a LESS-sparse concept (6 paper-hits) that the Run-24 sparsest-12 selection would NOT have deep-verified, yet a real functional gap survives -- a SACRIFICIAL/EXPENDABLE adapter that ABSORBS adversarial/distributional damage (is consumed itself) to PROTECT frozen backbone weights. I deliberately did NOT explain this gap away (R14): I searched 4 distinct framings (sacrificial adapter, decoy, honeypot/trapdoor, low-importance damage routing, robustness adapter). The honeypot/trapdoor work ('Gotta Catch Em All') is a GENUINE close neighbor and occupies the 'preferentially attract adversarial perturbation' half -- I record it honestly as a near-collision -- but its mechanism is DETECTION (the trapdoor is never consumed), not damage-absorption to spare weights, so the anode's defining 'corrodes instead of the protected metal' kernel remains unoccupied. Hence I rate C30 a SOFT but non-trivial GAP (composite 81, gate4 pass), with explicit residual uncertainty due to the honeypot neighbor. Skeptical both ways: I down-rated C29's TMD 'resonant-frequency' framing as an arbitrary over-specification (not a real gap) even though no frequency-tuned output damper exists, because there is no evidence LLM degeneration has a damp-able single resonant frequency, and the functional core is fully covered by contrastive decoding.
